title: Phased Release Circuit-Breaker and Regression Annotator for A/B and Progressive Rollouts
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Implement a phased-release circuit-breaker service that binds continuous eval signals to staged A/B and progressive rollouts and can automatically execute targeted rollback actions. This ticket builds a regression annotator that tags signals with likely root causes (model variant, config flag, quantization profile, routing policy) and a policy engine that enforces hysteresis and SLA-aware thresholds before aborting or reverting exposures. Goal: prevent noisy model/config changes from causing customer-visible quality regressions while providing actionable provenance for post-mortems.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Service emits an "eval_event" for each evaluation window containing multi-metric snapshot, baseline comparison, and root-cause tags

2) Policy engine supports per-release policy objects: metric thresholds, hysteresis windows, min-sample requirements, and rollback action (route revert, config flip, scale-down), and can be attached to any rollout
3) Automatic rollback executes within configured SLO (default 5 minutes) when policy is breached and escapes noisy signals via adaptive minimum sample size and baseline variance checks
4) Rollback actions are visible in Console rollouts UI and appear in the rollout timeline with links to evaluation snapshots and root-cause annotations
5) Integration tests cover synthetic-probe detection, shadow-traffic probes, and A/B split experiments with deterministic rollback outcomes
6) Playbook autogenerated entry for each auto-rollback with investigation pointers, affected cohorts, and suggested remediation steps
design_notes: Use existing evaluation infrastructure to compute metrics per cohort: BLEU-like quality proxies, perplexity delta, user-latency, and hallucination score
Root-cause annotator will correlate metric deltas with recent config/model attributes using a lightweight decision tree + rule engine (no heavy ML) to keep deterministic provenance
Policy engine will implement two-tier checks: fast signal (low-latency but conservative) and robust signal (higher-latency, stronger evidence) to avoid flip-flopping
Hysteresis: require metric breach for N consecutive windows OR cumulative effect size > X before triggering rollback
Provide a safe 'partial rollback' action that only re-routes a percentage of traffic away from variant before full revert to minimize customer impact
implementation_plan: 1) Extend eval pipeline to emit per-release snapshots to new eval_event Kafka topic
2) Build Regression Annotator microservice that subscribes to eval_event, enriches with release metadata and root-cause tags, writes to eval-index
3) Implement Policy Engine gRPC with CRUD for policy objects and evaluation webhook endpoint consumed by rollout controller
4) Rollout Controller integration: wire policy evaluation to the progressive-exposure controller; support 3 rollback actions: route-revert, config-revert, and degrade-to-compatible-model
5) Console: add rollout timeline entries, manual-override controls, and links to evaluation snapshots
6) Add e2e tests and chaos-sim scenarios to ensure no false-positive rollbacks under transient noise
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): enable on staging with synthetic workloads and shadow traffic (2 weeks)
Phase B (dogfood): enable for internal product teams with low-traffic canaries (1 week)
Phase C (limited prod): 1% traffic across 2 regions with strict min-samples and human-in-loop notification (2 weeks)
Phase D (auto): enable auto-rollback with tuned policies for tiered customers, monitor for 2 weeks before wider enablement
open_questions: What is default min-sample threshold for short-lived canaries where sample sparsity is expected?
How should we weight different metrics (e.g., hallucination vs latency) when they conflict in policy decisions?
Should root-cause tags include a confidence score and how would that be used in automatic decisions?
Who signs off on enabling auto-rollback for enterprise customers with SLA constraints?
